weaknesses: Log-free sup-norm rate is the headline result but is never explained or qualified (Abstract; Section 4.2 after the theorem; Discussion paragraph 2). Sup-norm rates under strict overlap normally carry a logarithm, so a reader will ask why none appears here and what happens as the overlap exponent grows. The proof shows the constant depends on gamma_max through E_Gamma = max{1, 2*beta*(gamma_max-1) + d*gamma_max} and on 1/(gamma_max-1) through the maximal inequality, so K diverges as gamma_max tends to infinity. Fix: add a paragraph after the theorem stating that (i) the log is absorbed because only about (b/a)^{2(gamma-1)} lowest-rank cubes sit at the common cap, (ii) K grows with gamma_max and the bound holds for a fixed compact range, and (iii) how this relates to the strict-overlap log rate. Also state that the pointwise lower-bound constant c_gamma is permitted to depend on x_0.

Assumption discussion is formulaic and does not address restrictiveness (Section 3.3). Each assumption gets a 'standard condition' sentence and a loosely matched citation (consistency and exchangeability cited to Kennedy et al., iid to Stone 1982, Hölder balls to Dorn). Nothing discusses: why beta > 1 is required and what happens for beta <= 1; that the estimator needs beta and B known (clipping, threshold h^{-2 beta}, mesh grid); that one constant B bounds both the mean and the sub-Gaussian proxy; why C >= 1 and c_f <= 1; how to read gamma (gamma near 1 versus large gamma, relation to strict overlap); or which propensity models satisfy the tail bound. Fix: add a 'Discussion of assumptions' subsection with one or two worked propensity examples, an interpretation of D_gamma, and a candid statement of which requirements are substantive (known beta, known B, density lower bound, uniform sub-Gaussian scale) versus technical.

The comparison with Dorn rests on an unverified transcription and is not conservative enough (Introduction paragraphs 6-7, Related work, Section 5.2, Appendix C). Three issues. (a) The transferred envelope D_gamma has conditional variance exactly sigma_min^2 in both arms, while the displayed source restriction is Var >= sigma_min^2; the abstract and introduction should say the transfer covers the homoskedastic Gaussian envelope at variance sigma_min^2, or the result should be extended to bounded heteroskedastic variance. (b) The failure of the local anti-concentration condition is established only for a specific pointwise propensity version and, in the Gaussian case, with constants C', M', L_0' chosen per gamma; 'strict enlargement' in the introduction should carry both qualifiers in the same sentence. (c) Appendix C.3 says the common-regression clauses 'give the model-family qualification relevant to the pointwise lower attribution printed in' Dorn's Theorem 1(i). This insinuates a defect in a cited lower bound on the strength of a trivial constant-estimator observation. Either state precisely what Dorn's lower bound quantifies over and how it differs, or delete the remark.

The 'family obstruction' material is trivial content given major billing (final clauses of the transfer proposition; the two Appendix C results on known-regression families). That a family with a single known treated curve has zero minimax miss probability is immediate from the constant estimator. It occupies two formal statements, two proofs, and a clause of a main proposition. Fix: reduce it to a one-sentence remark ('a minimax converse requires a rich family; ours is over P_gamma') and remove those clauses from the transfer proposition so that it states only the transfer.

The main proposition and key lemma are overloaded, and the paper's architecture hides its contribution. The transfer proposition bundles eight separate assertions (finiteness of L_*, class membership, expectation bound, family restriction, probability bound, Gaussian counterexample, known-curve triviality, a restated lower bound). The selected-mesh lemma bundles a generic maximal inequality with the mesh analysis. The proof of the main theorem then re-derives the count event, oracle candidate and MGF envelope already proved in that lemma, and the ordered-mass and selected-mesh proofs re-prove lambda_0 > 0 and the rank bound. Fix: split the proposition into (i) transfer, (ii) Gaussian geometry example, each with its own statement; make the ordered maximal inequality its own lemma; have the theorem's proof cite the lemmas instead of repeating them; move the proof of the main theorem ahead of the source-comparison appendix.

Framing of novelty relative to Dorn's estimator is thin (Introduction paragraph 6; Related work paragraphs 1-2). The paper acknowledges that Dorn already obtains the same rate, gamma-adaptivity and count-based mesh selection, so the incremental contribution is (a) dropping the local anti-concentration condition via equal-cell weighting, (b) an expectation rather than in-probability sup-norm bound, and (c) sub-Gaussian rather than Gaussian outcomes with a density lower bound rather than uniform design. This is never stated as a crisp list, and the thin-strip example does not show that an existing estimator fails on that geometry, only that an assumption fails. Fix: add an explicit contribution list, and either show that an unweighted local polynomial fit is ill-conditioned under the strip law (the vanishing second-moment limit suggests this) or state plainly that the example shows the assumption is not needed, without implying the earlier estimator fails.

weaknesses: claims_vs_assumptions earns 7/10 because the principal rate claims carefully preserve fixed constants, known smoothness, compact exponent ranges, and pointwise lower-bound quantifiers, but Related work incorrectly describes the full envelope as imposing bounded potential outcomes; replace that description with bounded treated means and conditional sub-Gaussian residuals, reserving bounded potential outcomes for the converse subclass.

positioning earns 8/10 because the Dorn comparison specifies assumptions, loss criteria, adaptation, and citation locators, but the repeated common-regression obstruction gives a basic family-richness observation disproportionate prominence; consolidate it into one appendix remark and make the main comparison about the enlarged treatment geometry and expected spatial-supremum guarantee.

assumption_discussion earns 6/10 because the assumptions receive clear operational interpretations but mostly formulaic assertions of standardness; expand Limitations and future work to discuss full-dimensional density coverage, known isotropic smoothness, uniform conditional sub-Gaussian tails, and how the constants behave near the overlap-range endpoints.

writing earns 5/10 because the estimator and main guarantee are accessible in the main text, but repeated definitions, repeated theorem summaries, and extensively expanded elementary proof steps obscure the statistical argument; consolidate the template definitions, shorten assumption commentary, and organize the appendices around reusable lemmas.

In Statistical explanation, give readers the decisive quantitative mechanism immediately: display the ordered mass bound, the capped rank-dependent variance envelope, and their maximal-error consequence; the current verbal account repeatedly announces the mechanism while postponing its usable mathematical content.
defects: Related work: “These envelopes impose bounded potential outcomes” contradicts the mean-and-residual restriction defining the full class; replace it with “These envelopes impose a bounded treated conditional mean and uniformly conditional sub-Gaussian residuals.”

Setup and assumptions: “1<\gamma_{\min}\le\gamma_{\max}<\infty” permits a singleton interval, whereas the main uniform theorem and front matter specify distinct endpoints; use the strict endpoint inequality for the maintained adaptation interval or explicitly distinguish the two conventions.
The caption “Treated response magnitude bound” describes only part of the displayed assumption, which also controls residual exponential moments; rename it “Treated mean and residual bounds.”

The intrinsic Hölder definition says “Here \(d\) is a nonnegative integer and \(\beta,L\in\mathbb R\)” after the setup fixes \(d\ge1\), \(\beta>1\), and \(L>0\); retain the maintained parameter domain in the reader-facing definition and place any broader formal domain in the verification material.

“Tensor interpolation nodes,” “Polynomial template and microcell width,” and “Polynomial template \(G_0\) and microcubes \(V_\ell\)” repeat the node, matrix, eigenvalue, width, and microcube definitions; merge them into one anchored construction, preserving the existing anchors through the presentation system.

The transition “we enumerate the tensor nodes by a single index from \(1\) to \(J\)” introduces a second indexing convention without selecting an enumeration; specify a fixed lexicographic enumeration once and use it throughout the construction and proofs.

The estimator algorithm says “compute the empirical equal-cell Gram matrix ... and ... coefficient estimate” without a cross-reference to their defining environment; add \(\cref{obj:synth_4}\) at this instruction.

The opening of The ordered treated-mass profile attributes “the scaled microcells” to \(\cref{obj:def:template}\), which defines reference microcubes; cite \(\cref{obj:def:mesh-selector}\) for the scaled cells and retain the template reference for their reference geometry.

The source smoothness definition ends with “using the source's convention,” leaving the distance convention implicit in the main transfer statement; specify Euclidean distance there, as the source-model appendix subsequently does.

The main transfer proposition introduces “the full Hölder-radius functional” without its explicit formula until the proof; define it at first introduction as the maximum of the derivative supremum bound and top-derivative seminorm.

The bounded testing lemma displays “\(\operatorname{KL}(P_{0,h},P_{1,h})\)” before the manuscript explains the notation, with the explanation appearing after the long proof; move the Kullback–Leibler gloss and convention before the lemma.
The main-result proof uses “\(\|\mathbb P_{0,n}-\mathbb P_{1,n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\)” without defining the total-variation convention; state the convention before applying Pinsker's inequality.
The local approximation proof uses “\(\alpha!\)” without stating the multi-index factorial convention; add \(\alpha!=\prod_i\alpha_i!\) to the setup notation.

The singleton lemma says “\(\Sigma^{\mathrm D}(\beta,L_0)\) specified in \(\cref{obj:lem:fixed-cube-holder-completion}\),” but that lemma specifies derivative inequalities rather than defining the named source class; reference its actual definition in \(\cref{obj:prop:dorn-a3-free-corollary}\), with the applicable parameter domain made explicit.

The template-conditioning lemma begins “Let \(d,m,n\) be nonnegative integers, let \(\beta\in\mathbb R\)” while invoking the candidate collection defined for \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge1\), and \(\beta>1\); align the reader-facing domains or provide an explicit extended candidate-collection convention.

The thin-strip construction says “Draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independently given \(X\)” but does not explicitly include \(A\) in that independence statement, although its proof uses a three-factor product kernel; state that \(A,Y(0),Y(1)\) are conditionally mutually independent given \(X\).

The selected-mesh proof attributes “\(0^{-1}=0\)” and “the zero matrix assigned as the inverse of a singular Gram matrix” to the equal-cell formula, whose definition is restricted to feasible meshes; remove these unused totalization conventions from this feasible-mesh argument.

The bounded testing definition foregrounds “The totalized construction uses the positive-part weights” before presenting the ordinary Bernoulli experiment; present the admissible probability construction first and move the extension across inadmissible parameters to the verification material.

The phrase “with these exact completion witnesses and response curves” in the bounded-pair proof introduces formalization vocabulary into the statistical argument; replace it with “with the constructed causal completions and response curves.”
The main theorem proof says “every Hölder response witnessing membership”; replace it with “every Hölder response satisfying the model restrictions.”

The final clause of the thin-strip proposition, “In particular, \(\mathcal P_\gamma\) contains a law whose full singleton-family Dorn predicate fails,” repeats the membership and failure already asserted for the explicitly constructed law; remove the clause and its repeated final proof step.

The common-regression zero-risk calculation is stated and proved in the transfer proposition, the known-regression lemma, and the fixed-family scope proposition; retain one statement and proof and replace the other copies with \(\cref{obj:lem:arbitrary-family-lower-obstruction}\).

The adaptive-minimax proof rederives the oracle candidate, simultaneous count concentration, ordered coefficient envelope, maximal inequality application, and logarithm absorption already established in the selected-mesh lemma; invoke \(\cref{obj:lem:selected-mesh}\) and retain only the additional approximation and risk-integration steps.

The source transfer proposition calls \(R_{\mathrm{pt}}\) “the bounded-response pointwise minimax risk of \(\cref{obj:def:risks}\),” although that definition uses the full conditional sub-Gaussian class; call it the causal-class pointwise risk and use separate notation for the bounded-potential-outcome subclass.

“Every source family ... satisfying ... restrictions ... is nonempty” obscures whether nonemptiness is a hypothesis or a conclusion; write “Every nonempty source family satisfying the cited restrictions is contained in \(\mathcal D_\gamma\).”

The common-curve clauses require “\(\mu_P(x)=\mu^\circ(x)\)” for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), while the source smoothness and statistical experiment are specified on the source cube; state the comparison on the source cube and restrict evaluation points accordingly, or explicitly define the ambient extensions.

The author footnote promises a verification appendix containing “scope, toolchain, commit,” but Verification note supplies neither a toolchain version nor a commit identifier; include those metadata and the promised declaration mapping, or narrow the footnote to the information actually provided.

The transfer verification footnote says “This result uses the cited conclusion” and locates Assumptions 1–2 without identifying the imported conclusion; name the precise externally supplied statement or transcription on which the transfer depends.
The Introduction repeats “The adaptive minimax guarantee is stated in \(\cref{obj:thm:adaptive-minimax}\)” after already explaining and referencing that theorem; delete the standalone sentence.

The roadmap ends with “proofs of the main results” after describing earlier appendices as proof appendices, and several earlier geometry and transfer subsections contain summaries rather than the promised proofs; identify the final proof appendix as the location of the complete main-result proofs and label the preceding sections as auxiliary arguments or comparison explanations.
